title: Why Is a Mushroom Not a Plant? Explained Simply | PUC Biology Class 11
description:
A mushroom grows from the soil and never moves, just like a plant. Yet biologists say it is not a plant. Diya finds one in the college garden after the rain and asks why. The answer is in the questions scientists ask before they place any living thing in a group.

You will see Aristotle's first sorting (trees, shrubs, herbs; animals with and without red blood), Linnaeus' two kingdoms, and a live two kingdom sort that breaks on a mushroom, a bacterium and Euglena. A zoom ladder takes the mushroom down to its hyphae, one hypha and its chitin wall, with every part labelled. Then the seven tests (cell type, cell wall, nuclear membrane, body organisation, mode of nutrition, reproduction, phylogenetic relationships), prokaryotic vs eukaryotic cells, a worked four-question key, the exam trap about cell walls, an original NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 11 of our PUC Biology series.
Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11 and NEET students.

In this video:

4:36 Exam trap: a cell wall means a plant?
4:57 Practice question (NEET pattern)
